classification.difficultyReason: The hardest part requires introducing an altitude in the isosceles triangle, using symmetry to halve its apex angle and base, then finding perpendicular lengths with trigonometry before calculating area. This construction is not supplied.

content.prompt: Find the area of each of the triangles shown below. Give answers to two decimal places.

spec.description: Unfilled right triangle with vertical left side 2.1 and angle 40 degrees at the bottom-right vertex.
spec.mathematics: Opposite side 2.1; adjacent base is 2.1/tan(40 degrees).
spec.answerVisibility: Only the source givens are visible.

answer.worked:
Let the base be $b$.
$$\begin{align*}\tan40^\circ&=\frac{2.1}{b}\\b&=\frac{2.1}{\tan40^\circ}\\A&=\frac12\times\frac{2.1}{\tan40^\circ}\times2.1\\A&\approx2.63\text{ square units}.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Unfilled right triangle with horizontal base 11 and angle 28 degrees at the right vertex.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the source givens are visible.

answer.worked:
Let the height be $h$.
$$\begin{align*}\tan28^\circ&=\frac{h}{11}\\h&=11\tan28^\circ\\A&=\frac12\times11\times11\tan28^\circ\\A&\approx32.17\text{ square units}.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Unfilled right triangle with hypotenuse 9, angle 36 degrees at the bottom-left vertex and right angle at the bottom-right vertex.
spec.mathematics: Base is 9 cos(36 degrees); perpendicular height is 9 sin(36 degrees).
spec.answerVisibility: Only the source givens are visible.

answer.short:
$19.26$ square units

Find the base and height using cosine and sine.
answer.worked:
Let the base be $b$ and height be $h$.
$$\begin{align*}\cos36^\circ&=\frac{b}{9}\\b&=9\cos36^\circ\\\sin36^\circ&=\frac{h}{9}\\h&=9\sin36^\circ\\A&=\frac12(9\cos36^\circ)(9\sin36^\circ)\\A&\approx19.26\text{ square units}.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Unfilled isosceles triangle with both sloping sides labelled 4 and included apex angle 100 degrees. No altitude is supplied.
spec.mathematics: A perpendicular from the apex bisects the base and apex angle, giving two right triangles with hypotenuse 4 and apex angle 50 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the source givens are visible.

answer.short:
$7.88$ square units

Bisect the isosceles triangle into two right triangles.
answer.worked:
Draw a perpendicular from the apex to the base. It bisects the base and the $100^\circ$ angle. Let the half-base be $b$ and height be $h$.
$$\begin{align*}\sin50^\circ&=\frac{b}{4}\\b&=4\sin50^\circ\\\cos50^\circ&=\frac{h}{4}\\h&=4\cos50^\circ\\A&=\frac12(2b)h\\A&=(4\sin50^\circ)(4\cos50^\circ)\\A&\approx7.88\text{ square units}.\end{align*}$$
